chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: How John Hammond tracked Fields down in Tulsa
summary: Hammond, after hearing of Fields in Kansas City, calls through a waiter at the Club Lido; Fields' wife relays the message after Hammond tips the waiter five dollars.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, you know, you told me a story earlier, and I'd like--now I think would be the appropriate time, how Willard and John Hammond got in touch with you. You see we talked about that but it's not on the tape.

To backtrack a little, it all came about before we went into New York, naturally Hammond had discovered Basie and I think he carried Harlan Leonard in New York City, a band out of Kansas City, and what's this trumpet player out of Kansas City--all of them had good bands but they just didn't click or something. Well, Hammond was still trying to find something else

that he could maybe turn national and he came to Kansas City again, and so while he was around Kansas City, he looked and he hadn't run into anything and asked some questions, and so somebody asked him if he ever heard of Ernie Fields' band. And he told him no. He said, is that a band here? He said no but he has a mighty fine band. So he said, where is he? He said he's an Oklahoma band, I think his headquarters are Tulsa, Oklahoma. He just comes in here and plays now and then.

So Hammond got to talking around and of course Yardbird and all the guys in jazz that knew about the Ernie Fields band because I had outstanding men, Luther West and all, they hung out together and all the bands and they would tell him that he's in Tulsa, Oklahoma. So Hammond comes to Tulsa.
He went to the Club Lido, a club in Tulsa and he got in touch with one of the waiters and wanted to know if he knew Ernie Fields and they told him yes, they knew Ernie,

So he said, how could I get a hold of him. He said, well, he has a telephone. So Hammond said would you mind calling him and he said yes and went and called me and I wasn't in, I was out on a gig that night. I remember that week and I was in a little hick town around. So he came back and told Hammond that I wasn't in, that I was playing that night. So Hammond told him again, go call and give him my room number, I'm in the May Hotel and tell him to call me when he gets up tomorrow morning.

So he came back and called my wife and told her to tell me and gave her his room number and the May Hotel telephone number and told her to tell me to call him. So she said okay, but John Hammond didn't mean any more to her than it meant to this waiter at that time. So when the waiter goes back to Hammond, Hammond thanked him and gave him a five dollar bill and he said I don't have the change; he said that's yours. So he comes back to the telephone a third time and he called my wife that third
time and said, Mrs. Fields, I don't know who that is, but you tell Ernie to be sure and contact that me, he apparently is somebody mighty big, he just gave me five dollars for spending a dime.
Five dollars was a fortune then.
